missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Раствор' is a masculine noun in the nominative as the subject. 'Этот' agrees, and 'прозрачный' describes the clear solution.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Раствор' is the accusative direct object of 'приготовил'; an inanimate masculine noun keeps its base form. 'Новый' agrees.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Раствора' takes the genitive after 'нет' to express that the solution is missing. 'В колбе' is the prepositional location.
Strategic focus: Dative after к. 'Раствору' is the dative form after 'к', marking what the salt was added to. 'Соль' is the nominative subject.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after с. 'Раствором' is the instrumental form required by 'с', the substance worked with. 'Этим' agrees in the instrumental.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'Растворе' takes the prepositional form after 'в' to mean inside the solution. 'Много соли' uses the genitive after 'много'.
Strategic focus: Genitive of possession. 'Раствора' is the genitive form expressing whose colour it is. 'Цвет' is the nominative subject, and 'зелёным' is instrumental after 'стал'.
Strategic focus: Genitive singular after numeral. 'Раствора' is genitive singular required by 'два'. 'В лаборатории' is the prepositional location.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural. 'Растворы' is the accusative plural object of 'приготовили'. 'Разные' agrees in the plural, describing the various solutions.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after много. 'Растворов' is the genitive plural required by 'много'. 'Старых' agrees in the genitive plural, and 'на полке' is locational.
